summary: KU Leuven's Science@Leuven Scholarship pays €12,000 a year for up to two years to excellent students from abroad who start a master's in its Faculty of Science, in subjects from physics, chemistry and mathematics to biology, statistics and sustainable development. Students from outside the EEA also pay a reduced tuition fee. It is open to every nationality except Belgian, and the deadline for 2027-28 is 15 February 2027.
meta_title: Science@Leuven Scholarship 2027-28: €12,000 a year at KU Leuven
meta_description: KU Leuven's Science@Leuven Scholarship: €12,000 a year and reduced tuition for a science master's. All nationalities but Belgian. Deadline 15 Feb 2027.
covers: An allowance of €12,000 per academic year, for up to two years if you do well in your first year.
A partial tuition waiver for students from outside the EEA, who paid €3,252.72 in 2026-27 whatever their programme. KU Leuven has not yet set the 2027-28 amount.
EEA students receive the allowance but no extra tuition reduction.
eligibility: Excellent results in your previous studies, equivalent to at least a Distinction at KU Leuven.
A bachelor's from a university outside Belgium that gives access to the master's.
No previous study or work at KU Leuven, and no master's or PhD already.
Strong English: an IELTS score of at least 7 overall, or the TOEFL equivalent, counts in the selection.
how_to_apply: Choose an eligible master's: Astronomy and Astrophysics; Biology; Biophysics, Biochemistry and Biotechnology; Chemistry; Mathematics; Physics; Statistics and Data Science; or Sustainable Development. Geography and Geology qualify only when KU Leuven is your home institution.
Apply for the master's in KU Leuven's online application tool and upload your transcript, a short description of your relevant courses, two reference letters and a motivation letter.
When the confirmation email for your programme application arrives, apply for the Science@Leuven Scholarship and add that email.
Finish both before 15 February 2027. KU Leuven ranks applicants in April and awards the scholarships at the beginning of May 2027.
watch_out: The number of scholarships changes each year with the funds available, and the selection committee usually interviews around eight applicants.
If it is clear you will not be admitted to the master's, your scholarship application is not considered.

From a lower-income country? The Faculty of Science fee waiver goes to every eligible student, with no competition, and lowers tuition to about €5,141.8 in 2027-28. Nationals of least developed and other low-income countries get it automatically; nationals of lower-middle-income countries such as India, Pakistan, Nigeria, Kenya and Ghana apply by 1 March 2027.
costs: You, at the reduced non-EEA rate (€3,252.72 in 2026-27)
documents: A transcript of records with ECTS credits and grades.
Half a page to a page describing the courses relevant to the master's.
Two reference letters from internationally renowned professors.
The confirmation email from your KU Leuven programme application.

faq.q: How much is the Science@Leuven Scholarship?
faq.a: €12,000 per academic year for up to two years. Students from outside the EEA also pay a reduced tuition fee, which was €3,252.72 in 2026-27.

faq.q: When is the Science@Leuven deadline for 2027-28?
faq.a: 15 February 2027. Applications opened on 1 October 2026, and the scholarships are awarded at the beginning of May 2027.

faq.q: Can students from any country apply?
faq.a: Every nationality except Belgian can apply, if your previous results equal at least a Distinction at KU Leuven and you have not studied or worked at KU Leuven before.
